title: Music Project Migration in Ardour
summary: Replace unavailable original instruments and effects in complete source-only Ardour projects, preserve editable music and routing, and deliver the full mix and per-track stems.
taskPrompt: Repair input/project/project.ardour on Linux. Preserve all original notes, muted editable material, controllers, tempo, meter, track organization and routing. Choose installed open-source replacement instruments/effects that approximate the original reference audio; generic GM assignment is not automatic acceptance. Save output/migrated_project/migrated_project.ardour and all media/plugin state, output/available_plugins.txt, output/overview.png, output/mixdown.wav and full-song solo WAVs in output/stems/<track_name>.wav. Export from time zero at 44.1 kHz or higher. Public rubric: software/rubric.txt. All five original registered variants and full workloads are retained.
agentMustDo: Replace unavailable active instruments/effects without deleting or transposing original music; disabled effects need no replacement.
Preserve original editable events, controller meaning, tempo/meter and routing; use editable instrument adapters when needed.
Save a self-contained native Ardour project, full mix, complete original per-track/channel solo stems and overview screenshot.

evaluation: Native save/reopen and original music/routing, required deliverables and a valid full mix are gates. Score: 20% valid full-length matched stems / all expected stems; 80% fixed audio-semantic rubric, averaged over three reference-selected 12s passages per active stem, then across active stems. Each passage is evaluated for both delivered and freshly native-rendered audio against the reference; the lower rating is used, so copied reference WAVs cannot hide incorrect native playback. Missing or invalid stems get zero in the unchanged denominator. Passage centers are 25/50/75% quantiles of 100ms reference RMS bins above -60dB relative to the loudest reference bin; duplicate windows are merged. Proven decoded PCM identity or one shared positive scalar consistent with analytic integer-PCM quantization bounds earns timbre 1; no lossy-format equality is presumed. Otherwise official gpt-audio-1.5 uses public rubric.txt, ratings 0..4 divided by 4. No MFCC fallback, whitelist or fitted timbre threshold. Effective simple CC state is compared rather than raw counts; native cumulative rounding up to 5 ticks at 1920 PPQ is reported, while bank/program/switch/stateful order remains checked. Runtime, reference, unassessable provider and unsupported-verifier failures are infrastructure errors, not candidate zeros. The judge has measured positive under-scoring; this integration does not establish broad perceptual reliability or accept the private GM diagnostic.
